about: Casting materials a housing may be made of: the values a design needs before it is simulated - density for mass, stiffness and strength for later - each with where it comes from. Minimum values from the standards; density and modulus typical. Check against the foundry's own before a design is released.

default.source: the ductile iron wind-turbine gearbox housings are cast in, when nothing says otherwise (assumed)

materials.name: grey cast iron EN-GJL-250
materials.source: EN 1561:2011 - minimum tensile strength; density and modulus typical

materials.name: ductile cast iron EN-GJS-400-18-LT
materials.source: EN 1563:2018 - minimum 0.2% proof and tensile strength; the grade wind-turbine housings are cast in for low-temperature toughness

materials.name: ductile cast iron EN-GJS-500-7
materials.source: EN 1563:2018 - minimum 0.2% proof and tensile strength

materials.name: ductile cast iron EN-GJS-600-3
materials.source: EN 1563:2018 - minimum 0.2% proof and tensile strength

materials.name: cast steel G20Mn5, quenched and tempered
materials.source: EN 10213:2016 - minimum 0.2% proof and tensile strength

materials.name: cast aluminium EN AC-42100 (AlSi7Mg0.3), T6
materials.source: EN 1706:2020 - typical T6 values for sand casting

min_wall_mm.source: a minimum for large sand castings in iron, when no material is chosen (assumed)

rib_to_wall.source: foundry rule of thumb: a rib no thicker than 0.8 of the wall it joins

hole_ligament.source: metal left between two holes, or between a hole and a rib or an edge, at least one plate thickness (assumed)

root_gap.source: clear gap between two ribs standing in the open at least twice the thinner: room for the sand between them (assumed)

rib_start.source: the engineer's starting point for a new variant of ribs: 20 mm thick, 100 mm apart, as tall as what they meet, two to ten of them; a root fillet, edge round and draft each of three choices, the middle one first
